records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn-absence assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey are swallowed no-ops because catch(Exception) also catches the AssertionError raised by fail(). In both blocks the test does assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"), nullValue()) inside a try and then fail(). If the webauthn form IS present, findElement succeeds, assertThat(...) throws AssertionError, which is caught by catch (Exception nsee) and silently discarded; if absent, fail() throws AssertionError which is likewise caught. Either way the test proceeds past the check, so the regression it claims to guard (passkeys UI leaking into re-auth for a user without passkeys) would pass CI without failing — the reviewer and future maintainers get false confidence that this behavior is covered.
records.rationale: The described mechanism is incorrect: the test uses `catch (Exception nsee)`, and JUnit/Hamcrest failures throw `AssertionError` (an `Error`), which is **not** caught by `catch(Exception)`. In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, if the WebAuthn form is present, `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` will throw an `AssertionError` that will *not* be swallowed by `catch (Exception nsee)` and the test will fail. The diff explicitly shows `} catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`, not `catch (Throwable)` or `catch (AssertionError)`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referenced method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (no-arg) is not defined anywhere in this diff for UsernameForm, so the diff relies on a helper whose provenance and semantics (realm check only, ignoring the current user) cannot be traced to any stated requirement here. If the helper is missing or resolves passkeys state differently than UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) (which takes a user and combines three conditions), the two authenticators diverge on the same decision and the re-auth flow renders inconsistent pages; reviewers and future maintainers cannot verify the invariant from this change alone.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() is hard-overridden to false, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm never populates the user's authenticator list on any conditional-UI page, including the error path createErrorResponse which still calls fillContextForm. A user whose webauthn authenticator is used with an identified user (2-factor or error re-challenge) gets a webauthn form with no authenticators rendered; after a failed passkey attempt the error page offers no list/button to retry with a specific credential, leaving the re-authentication flow stuck and pushing users to password fallback even when a passkey is their only usable credential.
records.rationale: The diff shows `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates authenticator-list population on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (changed from `if (user != null)`), and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` hard-overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(...)` to `return false;`. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webauthn form setup was moved out of the user==null branch but is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so on a fresh (non-reauth) login where no user is preset, fillContextForm is never invoked and the conditional-UI/discoverable-passkey data (previously set up for the anonymous username/password page) is no longer populated. Realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled lose discoverable-passkey autofill on the initial login page; first-time logins must fall back to password, which both degrades the phishing-resistant path and contradicts the test expectation that the //form[@id='webauth'] element be present for anonymous users (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey).

records.issue_text: [BUG] The second 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey has the same try/catch swallowing the AssertionError, and additionally the enclosing catch makes the fail() call unreachable whenever findElement succeeds. The re-authentication page assertion 'passkeys login should not be available as this user does not have a passkey' is unconditionally satisfied: both outcomes (element absent -> NoSuchElementException caught; element present -> AssertionError caught) lead to a passing test, so the core claim of this new test is never actually verified.
